questions.q: What does apt update actually do?
options: Refreshes the local list of available packages and versions from configured repositories — it doesn't install or upgrade anything by itself
Immediately installs the newest version of every package on the system
Removes all installed packages
Downloads an installer file you then double-click
questions.explain: apt update only updates apt's own knowledge of what's available; apt upgrade is the command that actually installs newer versions.

questions.q: Which package managers are used on RHEL, Fedora, CentOS, and Amazon Linux?
options: yum and dnf
apt and apt-get
npm and pip
chmod and chown
questions.explain: dnf (Dandified YUM) is the modern tool on these distros, with yum as the older one it replaced.

options: Lists available package updates without installing them
Installs every available update immediately
Uninstalls dnf itself
Checks the system's network connectivity
questions.explain: Like apt update, dnf check-update only refreshes/reports what's available — dnf update is the command that actually installs it.

questions.q: You SSH into an unfamiliar cloud VM and apt install curl fails with "command not found." What does that most likely tell you?
options: The VM is running a RHEL/Fedora/Amazon Linux-family distro, so you should try dnf install curl (or yum install curl) instead
curl cannot be installed on cloud servers
The VM has no operating system installed
apt is broken and needs to be reinstalled with dnf
questions.explain: A missing apt command is a strong sign you're on a yum/dnf-family distro rather than Debian/Ubuntu.

questions.q: Why does knowing both apt and yum/dnf matter in real cloud work?
options: Cloud roles routinely mix Debian/Ubuntu-based and RHEL/Fedora/Amazon-Linux-based servers in the same environment, often in the same week
Only one package manager is ever used across an entire company, so this is purely academic
yum and dnf are being retired industry-wide in favor of apt
Package managers are identical across all distros, so there's nothing extra to learn
questions.explain: A real cloud career puts you in front of both families regularly — an Amazon Linux EC2 instance here, an Ubuntu VM there, a legacy RHEL box somewhere else.
